set-payload.value: #[%dw 2.0 import bandOf, priceLadder from modules::HomeView output application/java var points = readUrl('classpath://samples/canonical-entsoe-quarterly.json', 'application/json') var ladder = priceLadder(points) fun countOf(label) = sizeOf(points filter (bandOf($.pricePerKWh, ladder) == label)) --- { cheap: countOf('CHEAP'), normal: countOf('NORMAL'), expensive: countOf('EXPENSIVE'), total: sizeOf(points) }]

munit-tools:assert-that.message: Every interval must fall in exactly one band.
CHEAP should cover roughly a third of the day.

munit:test.name: cheapest-interval-is-cheap-and-dearest-is-expensive
munit:test.description: The two unambiguous cases, asserted on real prices.

set-payload.value: #[%dw 2.0 import bandOf, priceLadder from modules::HomeView output application/java var points = readUrl('classpath://samples/canonical-entsoe-quarterly.json', 'application/json') var ladder = priceLadder(points) var sorted = points orderBy $.pricePerKWh --- { cheapestPrice: sorted[0].pricePerKWh, cheapestBand: bandOf(sorted[0].pricePerKWh, ladder), dearestPrice: sorted[-1].pricePerKWh, dearestBand: bandOf(sorted[-1].pricePerKWh, ladder) }]

munit-tools:assert-that.message: Fixture drift check: the captured day's cheapest quarter-hour.

munit:test.name: a-negative-day-mean-does-not-invert-the-bands
munit:test.description: The reason banding is by rank and not by percentage of the mean.

set-payload.value:
#[%dw 2.0 import bandOf, priceLadder from modules::HomeView output application/java var points = readUrl('classpath://samples/negative-price-day-hourly.json', 'application/json') var prices = points map $.pricePerKWh var ladder = priceLadder(points) var sorted = prices orderBy $ var dayMean = (prices reduce ((item, acc = 0) -> acc + item)) / sizeOf(prices) fun countOf(label) = sizeOf(points filter (bandOf($.pricePerKWh, ladder) == label)) --- { dayMean: dayMean, cheapestBand: bandOf(sorted[0], ladder), dearestBand: bandOf(sorted[-1], ladder), cheap: countOf('CHEAP'), normal: countOf('NORMAL'), expensive: countOf('EXPENSIVE'),
/* * What the REJECTED rule would have produced. Saving as a * fraction of the day's mean, for the cheapest hour of the * day. With a negative mean the division flips the sign, * so the cheapest hour reports as ABOVE the mean and a * percentage-based banding would call it EXPENSIVE. */ rejectedRuleSaving: (dayMean - sorted[0]) / dayMean }]

munit-tools:assert-that.message: This fixture is only meaningful if the day mean is negative.
Percentage-of-mean inverts here: the cheapest hour looks dearer than average.
The cheapest hour of a negative day is still the cheapest hour.

munit:test.name: the-covering-interval-is-half-open
munit:test.description: An instant on a boundary belongs to the interval it starts, not the one it ends.

set-payload.value: #[%dw 2.0 import covering from modules::HomeView output application/java var points = readUrl('classpath://samples/canonical-entsoe-quarterly.json', 'application/json') var boundary = points[1].startsAt as DateTime --- { boundary: points[1].startsAt, atBoundary: covering(points, boundary).startsAt, justBefore: covering(points, boundary - |PT1S|).startsAt, beforeTheDay: covering(points, (points[0].startsAt as DateTime) - |PT1H|) }]

munit-tools:assert-that.message: An instant exactly on a boundary belongs to the interval it STARTS.
One second earlier belongs to the previous interval.
An instant outside the published day is covered by nothing.
